{{Quote|I shouldn't have come back.|Padmé Amidala regrets the casualties caused by her return to Coruscant, including R2-H7|audio=Padme-ShouldntHaveComeBack-AOTC.flac|<ref name="AOTC" />}}
'''R2-H7''' was a [[Color|green]]-and-white [[R2-series astromech droid]] in the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces]] who traveled to the [[planet]] [[Coruscant]] in [[22 BBY]] in the [[astromech socket]] of an [[N-1 starfighter]] [[pilot]]ed by [[Captain]] [[Gregar Typho]]. The pair was part of an escort for [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]], whose [[J-type diplomatic barge]] was destroyed in an explosion when they reached Coruscant. Amidala survived, but R2-H7 was damaged by flaming debris from the blast.

==Biography==
{{Quote|We made it. I guess I was wrong, there was no danger at all.|Typho speaks too soon|audio=Typho-NoDanger-AOTC.flac|<ref name="AOTC" />}}
R2-H7 was an [[R2-series astromech droid]]<ref name="BMF 55" /> manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton]]<ref name="Manufacturer" /> that served in the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces|security forces]] that protected the [[Royal House of Naboo|Royal House]] of the [[planet]] [[Naboo]].<ref name="AOTC" /> In [[22 BBY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]'' dates the events of {{Film|II}} to [[22 BBY]].</ref> R2-H7 was in the [[astromech socket]] of an [[N-1 starfighter]] [[pilot]]ed by [[Captain]] [[Gregar Typho]] as he escorted the [[J-type diplomatic barge]] of [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] of Naboo to the planet [[Coruscant]], where the senator intended to vote in the [[Galactic Senate]] on the [[Military Creation Act]]. Upon arriving on Coruscant, Typho landed the [[starfighter]] on a landing pad as the barge parked nearby and then disembarked from the vehicle.<ref name="AOTC" />

[[File:R2-H7-Debris-AOTC.png|thumb|left|300px|R2-H7 was knocked down by flaming debris.]]
R2-H7 then also lowered from the fighter onto the platform as Typho met up with Amdiala, who had flown in disguise based on Typho's fear that returning to Coruscant might prove dangerous for her. His fears were proven correct when a [[bomb]] planted by the [[assassin]] [[Zam Wesell]] detonated and [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala|destroyed]] the barge, [[Death|killing]] Amidala's decoy, [[Cordé]]. Flaming debris spewed from the explosion, with one piece striking R2-H7 and damaging the [[droid]], knocking it over. R2-H7 was then left smoking on the ground as Typho and Amidala fled to safety.<ref name="AOTC" />

==Characteristics==
R2-H7 had [[Color|white]], green, and silver plating and a black [[sensor]].<ref name="AOTC" /> It stood 0.96 [[meter]]s (3[[Foot|ft]], 2in) tall.<ref name="Height" />

==Behind the scenes==
R2-H7 first appeared in the [[2002]] [[prequel trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']].<ref name="AOTC" /> The droid was a digital element added during the post-production of the film<ref name="BMF 55" /> and was first named by author [[Tim Veekhoven]]<ref name="Veekhoven">{{Twitter|Sompeetalay|status/1037318484919771137|[[Tim Veekhoven]]|quote=#BuildtheMillenniumFalcon: Added the name of R2-H7 (damaged green and white Astromech Droid at the explosion on Coruscant) [Issue 54: Senator Amidala's Transport]|archivedate=20220327114653}}</ref> in [[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 55|''Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon'' 55]], an issue of [[De Agostini]]'s ''[[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon]]'' magazine<ref name="BMF 55" /> published around [[January 20]], [[2016]].<ref name="BMFdate">{{BMFdates|55}}</ref>
